facts.name: Pete Connor — operator
facts.statement: Holds three simultaneous roles: CTG Workspace Super Admin (acting), platform builder, and sole signer for all workspace and project decisions under ADR-0033.

facts.name: Wider operating roster
facts.statement: Beyond the executive triad: Sharon (Ndanga), Tafara, and Amittai. All six plus Pete appear on the L10 attendee list and the org-wide 2FA enforcement notice.

facts.name: Ideal Customer Profile
facts.statement: Title × industry × seat-band: enterprise CX and IT-infrastructure leadership at 500–10,000+ seat contact centers across six-to-seven priority industries. Pains: vendor sprawl, commission opacity, contract complexity, cost-take-out pressure.

facts.name: ICP registry (ICP-REG-01 / sr-icp-v1)
facts.statement: The single versioned niche-definition artifact every scoring or counting system must cite by icp_version. Lives at ctg-signal-radar/src/backend/icp_registry.py. Motivated by an incident where two production systems disagreed on the same count.

facts.name: Buying moment
facts.statement: A time-boxed window rather than a segment: a newly-seated VP/SVP within their first 180–240 days. The moment expires at ~day 240, computed as a view over title_start_date.

facts.name: Partner taxonomy
facts.statement: Four partner classes: guru (independent CX consultant), referral_partner (agency/reseller), TSD (peer distributor), CTG-direct (served directly).

facts.name: Partner record grain is the LLC
facts.statement: A partner record is an LLC, never an individual. Stated as a modeling invariant in the triage frame, the commission frame, and the C2 hygiene spec; enforced by the LLC heuristic in commission validation and required by the manual onboarding playbook.

facts.name: Guru
facts.statement: A formal partner class, transacted as an LLC. Simultaneously: a Type value, a live HubSpot association label on Company↔Contact / Company↔Deal / Deal↔Partner, an enum of ~46–49 LLC names on Deal.guru (41% filled), and an access tier — gurus get View access to the full Partner Portal folder. The live association label contains a zero-width character that breaks exact-match filters.

facts.name: Referral partner
facts.statement: A partner attribution class distinct from Guru. Deal.referral_partner enumerates 70+ individual (person) names rather than LLCs (28% filled) — a grain inconsistency with the LLC invariant. Also the Partner custom object's internal name. The Deal→Partner association label is misspelled 'Refferal Partner'.

facts.name: Supplier
facts.statement: A technology vendor whose product CTG resells or advises on. Represented three ways at once: a Company with main_category set (~114), a Supplier custom-object record (217), and values in two Deal enums. 297 supplier folders exist in Drive across three owner accounts.

facts.name: HubSpot object model
facts.statement: Standard objects Company (0-2), Contact (0-1), Deal (0-3), Ticket (0-5) plus exactly four custom objects: Partner (2-170551626, internal name referral_partner, 104 records), Supplier (2-172421985, internal name suppliers, 217), Reveer Commission (2-225009958, internal name reveer_commissions, 433), Partner Commission (2-170551628, internal name commission, 2 — abandoned). Two further object types PARTNER_CLIENT and PARTNER_SERVICE exist with 0 records and are unreadable under granted scopes.
facts.source: projects/_hubspot/ctg-prm-crm-reconciliation/data/exports/2026-06-01/custom-objects.md § The four custom objects + Scope gaps

facts.name: Partners modeled as Company-with-property
facts.statement: ADR-0016: partner LLCs are HubSpot Company records distinguished by a Type single-select whose ADR-decided values are {guru, referral_partner, TSD, supplier, customer} — never a Custom Object. Referral, Commission and Lead Registration ARE Custom Objects associated to that Company. Separately, the standard HubSpot Company `type` enum observed in the portal is PROSPECT/PARTNER/RESELLER/VENDOR/OTHER (docs/schema-probe-result.md § 1) — a different field from the ADR's decision.

facts.name: Double-entry / built-twice
facts.statement: Partner, supplier, and commission data are recorded simultaneously in flat Deal fields and in custom objects, with no working sync. Of 1,039 deals: partners 401 flat-only / 55 object-only / 115 both; suppliers 696 flat-only vs 1 object-only; commissions 681 flat-only vs 0 object-only.

facts.name: Broken bridge (0%-filled mirror fields)
facts.statement: The Deal mirror fields guru_partner_record_id/_name/_email, referral_partner_record_id/_email, and supplier_id are all ~0% filled: the object→Deal auto-copy never fired because its writer workflows are disabled.

facts.name: Commission record
facts.statement: A HubSpot custom object built by Impulse Creative. Each closed-won deal should carry one or more summing to 100% (±0.01), associated to partners via the 'Commission Recipient' association label.

facts.name: Protected surfaces
facts.statement: Fields never touched by any sync or archive: `*__` double-underscore fields (CTG's commission-amount convention), `Koalify*` fields (owned by the dedup integration), and supplier_id (read by live workflow 2599541488).

facts.name: GoldenRecord
facts.statement: The provenance-tagged output of enrichment fusion: one adjudicated authoritative value per field with confidence tiering. Produced by ctg-enrichment-dispatch, stored in Firestore in ctg-hs-exec-tool.

facts.name: AIR (account_intelligence_record)
facts.statement: One row per company_id per snapshot_date in BigQuery dataset ctg_account_intelligence. The fused feature record underneath the BQML model suite, drawing read-only from eight upstream sources.

facts.name: Seven canonical types
facts.statement: EmailMessage, CalendarEvent, Document, File, Spreadsheet/SpreadsheetRange, LLMResponse, AuditEvent. Every connector translates into these at the boundary; no raw Google JSON survives past the connector. AuditEvent is the only one written to a persistent store.

facts.name: EOS domain objects
facts.statement: Rocks (quarterly), Scorecard measurables (weekly), Issues (worked via IDS), To-Dos, Accountability-chart entries, decisionProposals/decisions, testingProjects.

facts.name: Enterprise insurance client (ISA counterparty)
facts.statement: An enterprise insurance client issued a 23-requirement Information Security Addendum to its MPSA. CTG is the audited vendor; a second deal is gated on the same audit-readiness posture.

facts.name: Named subprocessors
facts.statement: Google (platform), HubSpot (CRM), Anthropic (AI tooling). An external accountant holds tenant access with no DPA; a CRM vendor holds production admin on the CRM and was absent from any third-party register.

facts.name: Recurring external counterparties
facts.statement: Impulse Creative (PRM build), Flywheel (33-workflow HubSpot estate), Valley/joinvalley.co (CRM data sync), Impartner and Channeltivity (PRM alternatives evaluated), HubSpot CSM, Have Strategies (content).

facts.name: Peer TSDs
facts.statement: Telarus, Avant, Intelisys. Treated as benchmark peers rather than enemies; never named or shaded in buyer-facing material. A former advisor-ranking model over them was deprecated by the 2026-07-23 supplier pivot.

facts.name: Supplier catalog footprint
facts.statement: 421 supplier listings across 62 categories in the advisor-match catalog; 250+ technology suppliers, 40+ BPO providers, and 500+ additional vendors via strategic distribution in the constants registry.
facts.source: projects/advisor-match/README.md § intro; projects/ctg-advisor-v1.0.0/methodology/constants-registry.md § Supplier and partner footprint

facts.name: CRM volumes
facts.statement: Counts move materially across the audit window. 2026-06-01: 43,977 contacts / 21,608 companies / 1,039 deals. 2026-06-04: 43,946 / 24,854 (a real Jun-3 import of ~+3,246). 2026-06-16/17: 43,799 / 24,959 / 1,058.

facts.name: Voice profile
facts.statement: A ctg-voice-profile-l1-v1 record carrying tone, sentence lengths, openers/signoffs, framings, banned-vocabulary additions, and do/don't lists. Role-layer profiles live in code; individual profiles in Firestore.

facts.name: Content-asset types
facts.statement: Blog (CIO/VP CX, top of funnel), Case Study (buyer's peer, mid), White Paper (technical evaluator + procurement, mid-late), Channel Piece (peer-to-peer for sub-agents and peer TSDs).

facts.name: Kill switches
facts.statement: Every integration has a named kill switch (email_agents, icp_scoring, data_cleanup, hubspot_classifier, churn_prediction). Disabled means 503 or short-circuit. A CTG admin must be able to flip one within 60 seconds.

facts.name: DLP attestation (fail-closed)
facts.statement: Every LLM-bound payload passes Cloud DLP content:deidentify first. The LLM call site requires an X-Redacted: cloud-dlp:v1:<rule-set-hash> header and fails closed if it is absent. A regex fallback fires only above a monthly DLP cost ceiling, and alerts when it does.

facts.name: EMAIL-12 — hash-only LLM logging
facts.statement: Every LLM interaction logs SHA-256 hashes of prompt and response. Raw content is never persisted. AuditEvent is the only canonical type written to a persistent store.

facts.name: PII never in audit logs
facts.statement: Logs carry HubSpot IDs only — never names, emails, or phones. Banking details, SSNs, and commission amounts never appear anywhere outside HubSpot itself.

facts.name: Track A / Track B PII boundary
facts.statement: Track A is IDs, schema, and counts only, and commits to git. Track B is record-level PII, gated on explicit per-run go-ahead, with output to a gitignored data/exports/<date>/backup/ that is never committed. Enforced in code by bin/metrics_lib.py: page_ids/search_count/batch_assoc are Track A; batch_read/batch_assoc_to are Track B.

facts.name: Three run modes
facts.statement: HUMAN (Pete only; agents pre-stage and verify), GATED (propose → approve → execute verbatim → verify), UNATTENDED (read-only by construction). An agent hitting a HUMAN step returns BLOCKED and never improvises.

facts.name: Non-delegable list
facts.statement: Permanently human-only: interactive auth, break-glass, lockout-radius enforcement flips, destructive or irreversible operations, all credential handling, Drive sharing and corpus-allowlist signing, incident-response judgment calls, billing, BYOD consent. Agents never run deletes even after approval.

facts.name: Approval token
facts.statement: The literal string `APPROVED <TASK-ID>` from the operator is the only thing that converts a proposal into an execution. Questions, edits, and silence are not approval. A denied proposal is a constraint, not a retry target. An agent asking for approval is not an agent granting it.

facts.name: Evidence-gate doctrine
facts.statement: 'A control without a dated artifact is OPEN.' Status vocabulary is fixed: MET / PROPOSAL READY / NOT MET / BLOCKED / OPEN. 'Nothing is ever basically done.' Raw output lives in evidence/, never inline.

facts.name: Policy-vs-practice rule
facts.statement: 'Policy documents state what CTG requires; they are never evidence of what CTG does.' Present-tense control claims must match verified tenant state or move to STMT-01 with an owner and a date. The client's audit right under §2 covers exactly that difference.

facts.name: Evidence standard
facts.statement: Every control claim must trace to platform telemetry or a dated artifact; confidence is measured against outcomes, never self-reported. The ISA rule: state what CTG does, never what it requires. In the portfolio audits, every readiness number must trace to a file an auditor read; ungrounded cells are marked unverified; journal.jsonl beats rendered docs on disagreement.

facts.name: Two lanes
facts.statement: The Pete lane covers everything configurable and evidenceable in-tenant, with no budget. The Fred lane covers spend, personnel behavior, contracts, insurance, and CEO-only decisions. Confusing them is named 'the primary failure mode'.

facts.name: Material-breach traps
facts.statement: Two contract clauses carry explicit material-breach penalties: undisclosed AI under §1, and a missed §3(c) remediation deadline. Governance rule: never sign the AI attestation until the disclosure is actually delivered; never sign early to hit a date.

facts.name: Forensic evidence integrity
facts.statement: Evidence carries SHA-256 manifests, read-only method statements ('no tenant state modified'), MUTATION-LOGs for any change, and preserved-unaltered disposition trails. A canonical committed copy is designated when working copies exist.

facts.name: Confidentiality rule
facts.statement: Exact prior-year ARR, valuation multiple, member-LLC and cap-table names, and the ownership restructuring must never be quoted in shipped content. Skills cite 'per CTG brief §<section>' instead.

facts.name: Content review gate
facts.statement: Required blog elements (title ≤60, meta ≤155, CTA, 2 internal links, schema.org); legal review on defined triggers (supplier quotes, comparisons, commission figures, compliance claims); a human reviewer for the first 60 days then spot-check; buyer written sign-off for any case study. The engine refuses when a required spec input is missing.

facts.name: Revenue pre-send gate
facts.statement: No proposal or battlecard reaches an external channel without a ctg-brand-keeper neutrality/voice PASS followed by explicit human approval. Every Gmail touch is create_draft, never send. Phone and cold-call are refused outright on TCPA/FCC grounds.

facts.name: LinkedIn ToS posture
facts.statement: Programmatic LinkedIn sending, third-party LinkedIn automation, scraping, and commingling LinkedIn member data are permanently prohibited. A CI grep gate enforces zero LinkedIn API surface. The accepted-risk decision was Fred's and was DECLINED 2026-06-30, converting the program to an email-only launch.
facts.source: projects/ctg-hubspot-SDR/PROJECT.md § Out of scope; projects/Jess-SDR/PROJECT.md § Constraints

facts.name: Deliverability caps
facts.statement: Encoded, not advisory: email starts ≤20/day/inbox ramping to ~50 over 3 weeks, scaling via more inboxes; the SDR engine caps at ≤150 emails/inbox/day with bounce <2%. Sends run under a designated rep mailbox with a kill switch, per-inbox daily cap, and a deliverability gate (SPF/DKIM/DMARC plus warm-up).
facts.source: projects/Jess-SDR/PROJECT.md § Constraints; projects/ctg-hubspot-SDR/PROJECT.md § Success criteria; decisions/adr/0003a-gmail-send-dwd-scope.md § Decision 3

facts.name: Passive reads never write
facts.statement: The sentiment add-on emits guidance text only; passive reads never write to the mailbox. A rule dated from the 2026-07-01 incident.

facts.name: Deny-by-default command allowlist
facts.statement: A longest-prefix command policy where anything unlisted is refused: 73 commands (31 read, 24 write, 18 destructive).

facts.name: One writeback property
facts.statement: Account Intelligence may write exactly one new HubSpot property (ctg_account_intelligence_score, optionally ctg_recommended_action) and never overwrites source projects' ctg_* properties. Each ctg_* property is owned exclusively by its emitting project; ownership never crosses projects.

facts.name: Pete's Corner doctrine (enforced)
facts.statement: The editor hard-blocks saves that violate doctrine: GA without all four gate conditions, 'crosses perimeter' without a named mitigation, or 'ongoing'/'TBD' milestones.

facts.name: Legal layer is non-overridable
facts.statement: In the voice compiler, layers compile general → specific and later layers may restyle earlier ones, but layer 2 (legal/compliance) is non-overridable and banned vocabulary only accumulates, never subtracts. Validation failures flag rather than block — except layer-2 legal violations, which withhold the body.

facts.name: LEFT/RIGHT vault boundary
facts.statement: The vault enforces a LEFT (identity, voice, reference — read-only to agents) versus RIGHT (agent-writable) permission boundary in code via a centralized vault gateway, not by convention.

facts.name: Knowledge base is read-only
facts.statement: The knowledge-base folder is read-only by default — no edits to INDEX, references, ADRs, or cloned repos without explicit request. Consumption routes via INDEX.md; never crawl. The KB knowledge product's phase-01 integrity gate was a git status check proving zero diffs to knowledge-base/ and decisions/.

facts.name: Cleanup discipline
facts.statement: Files are never deleted; superseded content is quarantined by move to _archive/<topic>-<date>/ with a provenance README and restore command. Separate-remote inner repos get an in-place SUPERSEDED marker instead. archive/ holds preserved history and is not modified. Deletion is the operator's call.

facts.name: Docs-MCP-first (HARD RULE)
facts.statement: Any planning touching Google Workspace APIs must query the workspace-developer MCP first; anything touching HubSpot must query the HubSpot Developer MCP first. Never training-data knowledge — HubSpot ships changes weekly. The two sitemaps are navigation indexes, not sources of truth.
facts.source: CLAUDE.md § Google Workspace Documentation / § HubSpot Developer Documentation

facts.name: Verify hook assists, never blocks
facts.statement: The estate PostToolUse verify hook feeds check failures back as additionalContext so the model self-corrects. The hook never blocks.

facts.name: Over-report for the first month
facts.statement: Trust ramps by over-reporting: post everything to #crm-ops-review for the first month even when auto-executing. An automation type drops to summary-only after a month with zero corrections.

facts.name: GSD root exclusion
facts.statement: The workspace root has no GSD phase structure. /gsd:finalize and milestone/dependency/UAT audits must not be run at the root.

facts.name: Policy adoption gates
facts.statement: Policy drafts cannot leave v0.1 until 8 named governance decisions (framework anchor, inventory, device posture, insurance, incident roles, contractor scope, contract commitments, counsel) are answered, plus legal review and CEO signature. Counsel review is a hard gate before external distribution.

facts.name: Document register governance
facts.statement: EXT-00 defines per-document owner, approver, version, effective date, and next review. Material changes increment the version and require CEO re-approval; annual review applies. Self-certification statement items must match the claim ledger or be removed/restated with a committed date.

facts.name: Estate Sentinel anti-delegation
facts.statement: Operator-only: merging PRs, editing ADRs or known-issues memory, handling the Slack webhook URL, and declaring a KNOWN-DOWN service recovered. Outward actions (Slack posts, PR opens) only in explicitly invoked runs. Known-issues are synthesis-stage annotations only — a known-down service appears in every report as DOWN-KNOWN; detection is never skipped and rows are never dropped.

facts.name: Self-audit discipline
facts.statement: The positioning document was itself claim-ledgered before circulation. Conclusion: internal evidence-gated claims held (0 unsupported), while freshly-authored market prose failed (2 unsupported, 6 overstated). 'The discipline does not transfer by osmosis; it transfers by running it.'

facts.name: Sharon — data-input policy and supplier handoff
facts.statement: Owns the data-input policy going forward — what fields are required, what format, what validation runs on input. Also owns the supplier-facing URL handoff (routed through Darren's account) and is the human gate on the Telarus registration draft.

facts.name: No CFO voice by design
facts.statement: There is deliberately no CFO persona and no CFO-gap flag. Darren carries the commercial-finance voice, and the three-voice surface is canonical rather than a reduced four-voice form.

facts.name: Fred's delegation map
facts.statement: Fred delegates scheduling to Sharon, vendor payments/W-9s/invoicing to Jessica, and pipeline follow-up plus relationship nurturing to Darren. A plan that forces Fred into the weeds is treated as a broken plan. Jessica is net-receiving delegation from both and delegates out to no one.

facts.name: Commitment direction model
facts.statement: The ledger encodes decision direction explicitly: `Pete→X` means Pete owes X; `X→Pete` means Pete is waiting on X; `Pete→—` means Pete's own call to make.

facts.name: The operator gates executives too
facts.statement: Release gates run upward as well as downward. Jessica requested a training walkthrough on modules Pete had marked built; Pete gated it on A/B testing plus a GA tag first, and Jessica agreed. Separately, Pete advised against Jessica's requested HubSpot write-bot on scope, guardrails, and cost grounds; it was parked by mutual agreement rather than executed.

facts.name: Client-held rights
facts.statement: The enterprise client holds audit rights (§2), sole discretion over §3(b) substitution, approval over affected-party incident communications (§17), and issuance of the periodic TPRM assessment.

facts.name: Impulse Creative coordination required
facts.statement: IC's commission automation HubSpot workflows must not be modified. Any commission-touching automation is coordinated with IC, and the C5 automation gates on IC's build being live.
facts.source: projects/ctg-ops-automation/CLAUDE.md § Do-not-touch; README.md § What's NOT here yet

facts.name: The unsigned CRM decision register
facts.statement: All 13 decisions (D-01..D-13) in the CRM ratification pack carry blank dispositions and the signature block is unfilled. Phase 2+ execution is gated on every row carrying a disposition.

facts.name: Fred decision register D1–D5
facts.statement: The GTM program keeps a named Fred decision register: credit cap, grounding spend envelope, program sequencing, first Everyone-facing rollout, verify-before-build gates. D1–D4 were answered 2026-07-10.

facts.name: Decisions reserved to Pete alone (M05/M06)
facts.statement: Four: ratify the credit ratio, set contact-resolve trigger policy, resolve M06 milestone numbering, and name the SDR sequencing tool.

facts.name: Activation grant owner pairs
facts.statement: gmail.send scope = Fred + Jessica; labeled email sample = Pete + Fred; provider data keys = Pete procures, Fred approves; Shared Drive creation = Pete builds, Fred grants; external advisory-plugin ship = Jessica/counsel final nod before first client.

facts.name: Decisions carry an explicit flip condition
facts.statement: 'If the consolidation can't hold a named owner and a staged sequence — if it turns into a big-bang rebuild — the recommendation flips to harden in place and consolidate one pair at a time.'

facts.name: First live infrastructure run is operator-gated
facts.statement: 99-new-project.sh is a deliberate reviewed Pete action, never invoked by CI, hooks, or another script, and must never run without --project= before a manual spot-check.

facts.name: Decision ratification is server-enforced human
facts.statement: In the L10 tool, proposals are extracted automatically but only a human ratify/discard click creates a decision of record — enforced by Firestore rules making the collections server-write-only.

facts.name: The client security document set
facts.statement: The deliverable the whole governance layer exists to produce: a 10-file package — EXT-00 register plus EXT-01..EXT-07 (Information Security, Data Classification & Handling, Incident Response, Remote Work, Acceptable Use, Vendor & Third-Party Risk, Business Continuity) plus STMT-01 Security Status & Control Summary and STMT-02 Penetration Testing Status. The register enumerates 9 documents; the tenth file is the register. The EXT/STMT ID scheme is used inside the shipped documents, not only in the internal repo.

facts.name: Five-way audience tiering
facts.statement: The delivery vault is tiered into six folders carrying an explicit 'who it is for' column across five audiences: Everyone; Clients + prospects + leadership; Leadership; CEO-only; Leadership-only (raw data and internal). Documents are placed by audience, not by topic.

facts.name: Status vocabulary is translated at the client boundary
facts.statement: The fixed internal vocabulary (MET / PROPOSAL READY / NOT MET / BLOCKED / OPEN) does not cross the client boundary. External documents use 'In progress / Scheduled / Prepared'. The doctrine survives the translation — every in-progress item still carries an owner and a dated target — but the words change.
